top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) are a measured result that nature answers back to: independent clocks agree at the 1e-18 level, with centimetre-scale gravitational redshift and sharper bounds on varying constants and ultralight dark matter. Magic-wavelength trapping is a distinct idea from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes, and the two-name credit is defensible name by name. The lineage and priority points still need an expert check. P002 (magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene) is a real, experimentally confirmed prediction but is only eight years old, its pairing mechanism is unresolved and Yuan Cao is left out of the credit, so I rank it second. No award is last because there is a mature, defensible achievement to honour.
